semantics.reset: active-high asynchronous ar; assertion clears q to zero independently of clk; reset dominates data capture
semantics.capture: At each rising clk edge with ar low, q takes d using a nonblocking assignment
semantics.hold: q holds between rising clock edges unless reset is asserted; reset release alone does not capture d
semantics.initialization: No explicit initialization; q is unspecified until reset assertion or first rising clock edge

numeric.data: Single bit copied exactly; no arithmetic, signedness conversion, rounding, saturation or overflow

verification.method: Independent directed self-checking testbench with observations after nonblocking updates
cases: Asynchronous reset assertion while clk is static and q is one
Both zero and one data capture on rising edges
Data changes and falling edges do not change q
Reset held high overrides rising-edge data capture
Reset release does not capture data
Data capture resumes after reset release
verification.tools: Icarus Verilog v12, -g2012, explicit dev_tb top, finite compile and simulation timeouts

specification_ambiguities.detail: Reset polarity and reset value are not explicitly stated
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Interpret ar as conventional active-high asynchronous clear to q=0
